items.heading: Where a Genuine MBA Lateral
items.text: Where a genuine MBA lateral-entry route exists, the logic mirrors the engineering version in spirit: you are given credit for prior study or relevant experience, and you join the program partway through instead of starting over from year 1. The details, however, vary far more than they do in engineering.

rows: You join directly in year 2 (or a later semester) of a 2-year MBA/PGDM, skipping year 1 coursework.
You complete both years, from foundational subjects in year 1 through specialisation in year 2.

Candidates who finished year 1 of a related PGDM/Masters elsewhere, or who hold a 4-year BTech/BBA and meet the institute's own bridge criteria; some programs also weight 2-5 years of work experience.
Any graduate with a recognised bachelor's degree, usually 50%+ marks, who clears an entrance exam.
Varies widely by institute; some run their own test or interview, some accept CAT/MAT/CMAT scores, some skip a formal exam entirely.
CAT, XAT, GMAT, CMAT, or MAT, depending on the institute tier.
1 to 1.5 years at the specific institute, sold as a time-saver.
2 years, matching UGC guidance for a standard MBA.
